title: Galatians 1: chapter overview
paragraphs: The apostle Paul asserts his apostolic character against such as lessened it.
He reproves the Galatians for revolting from the gospel of Christ under the influence of evil teachers.
He proves the Divine authority of his doctrine and mission; and declares what he was before his conversion and calling.
And how he proceeded after it.

context: The churches in Galatia were formed partly of converted Jews, and partly of Gentile converts, as was generally the case.
attribution: Matthew Henry, Concise Commentary (public domain). Historical Protestant interpretation; other traditions may read these passages differently.

title: Galatians 2: chapter overview
paragraphs: The apostle declares his being owned as an apostle of the Gentiles.
He had publicly opposed Peter for judaizing.
And from thence he enters upon the doctrine of justification by faith in Christ, without the works of the law.

title: Galatians 3: chapter overview
paragraphs: The Galatians reproved for departing from the great doctrine of justification alone, through faith in Christ.
This doctrine established from the example of Abraham.
From the tenor of the law and the severity of its curse.
From the covenant of promises, which the law could not disannul.
The law was a school master to lead them to Christ.
Under the gospel state true believers are all one in Christ.

title: Galatians 4: chapter overview
paragraphs: The folly of returning to legal observances for justification.
The happy change made in the Gentile believers.
The apostle reasons against following false teachers.
He expresses his earnest concern for them.
And then explains the difference between what is to be expected from the law, and from the gospel.

title: Galatians 5: chapter overview
paragraphs: An earnest exhortation to stand fast in the liberty of the gospel.
To take heed of indulging a sinful temper.
And to walk in the Spirit, and not to fulfil the lusts of the flesh: the works of both are described.

title: Galatians 6: chapter overview
paragraphs: Exhortations to meekness, gentleness, and humility.
To kindness towards all men, especially believers.
The Galatians guarded against the judaizing teachers.
A solemn blessing.
